source.name: IA4S AR16 to ESRS DR fine mapping (ESRS 2023)

methodology: Each selectable AR16 sustainability matter is mapped to explicit ESRS 2023 Disclosure Requirements rather than whole standards. The mapping uses ESRS Set 1 disclosure structure and the EFRAG IG 3 datapoint corpus to keep topic-level scope at Disclosure Requirement level. Matter-agnostic requirements within a material standard apply across the relevant matters of that standard, while metric requirements are assigned only where the matter subject is covered by the requirement and supporting datapoints. Matters without a dedicated metric requirement retain the common requirements for their standard and are not padded with unsupported disclosure requirements.
limitations: The ESRS delegated regulation is authoritative if it differs from the supporting datapoint corpus. The mapping expresses binary topic-to-Disclosure Requirement applicability and does not assign materiality weights, thresholds, assurance conclusions, or legal interpretations. It is intended to scope platform datapoint collection and report-package preparation, with human confirmation of materiality remaining part of the workflow.

mappings.ar16_topic_label: Climate change — Adaptation to climate change
mappings.ar16_topic_label_es: Cambio climático — Adaptación al cambio climático
mappings.rationale: ESRS E1 matter-agnostic DRs apply to every material climate matter: IRO process (E1.IRO-1), material IROs and resilience (E1.SBM-3), climate in remuneration (E1.GOV-3), policies (E1-2), actions (E1-3) and targets (E1-4; MDR-T covers GHG and any other climate target). E1-9 added: its datapoints quantify assets and revenue at material physical climate risk and the effect of adaptation actions. Mitigation-specific DRs (E1-1 transition plan, E1-6 GHG, E1-7 removals, E1-8 carbon pricing) and the energy metric (E1-5) are not pulled in by adaptation alone.
